newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka Tamil rebels said offering prisoner swap.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka Tamil rebels said offering prisoner swap.

text.p: A group of Sri Lankan servicemen captured by Tamil Tiger rebels said on Friday that they had been offered freedom in exchange for guerrillas held by the military.
The 22 prisoners sent a letter, a copy of which was obtained by Reuters, to opposition leader Ranil Wickremasinghe asking him to help secure their release.
But a spokesman for Wickremasinghe said he had not received the letter and was unaware of the proposed prisoner swap.
The International Committee of the Red Cross, which has been a mediator in previous prisoner exchanges, declined comment.
A military spokesman said he was unaware of the letter or plans to exchange prisoners of war.
Overseas spokesmen of the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) were not available for comment on the letter.
Among the 22 was a naval officer captured by the Tigers when they sank his patrol vessel in a suicide attack in late 1994, on the eve of abortive peace talks with the government.
The letter quoted rebel leaders as saying the group had proposed to the government that the 22 prisoners be exchanged for three guerrillas captured by the military.

It said the LTTE wants the release of a rebel identified as "Kennedy" who was captured in an attack on an airbase and two female rebels known as "Mala" and "Uma" who were seized after a guerrilla attack on a navy base in the north. The rebels were captured last year.
The LTTE is fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the north and east of the predominantly Sinhalese Indian Ocean island.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the ethnic war, now in its 14th year.
